deliverables: kaggle/record_vae/ (CPU kernel for the stage B reference)

validation.name: stage A: every recorded call of the tiny decoder replayed through MLX (float32, weights moved to the MLX layout by the converter's rules); the mid-block Attention is covered through the mid block
causal padding on a distinct-integer tensor (replicate: 2 frames in front, none behind, 1 row/column per spatial side)
upsample: frame counts 1 + f_t (T - 1) and values for T in {1, 2, 7}, factors (1,2,2) and (2,2,2)
released structure (4 up blocks of 3 resnets, x8 spatial, x4 temporal, mid attention) at a small width vs live torch decode; T = 7 runs the default framewise temporal tiling
validation.criterion: shapes equal; rel_max <= 1e-4; also with framewise decoding off

validation.name: released config builds the reference decoder parameter names and shapes (converted conv layout)
stage B harness on a tiny VAE saved and converted like the real one (record_video_real.py, 7 latent frames)

stage B: real Lite-distill VAE (HF e4d652b7, SHA-256 c90f898a...), MLX float32 vs the released diffusers VAE in torch CPU float32 on Kaggle (kernel applehawk/k6-lite-distill-vae-reference v1, pinned c363d7c), Smoke latents [1,7,32,54,16], default framewise decoding
validation.criterion: rel_l2 <= 1e-3, PSNR >= 40 dB, peak memory recorded (stop above 24 GB)

validation.name: chunked causal conv equals one pass (1 output frame per chunk)

deviations.what: decode reproduces the reference's default framewise temporal tiling (use_framewise_decoding=True: tiles of 5 latent frames, stride 3, 4-frame linear blend) instead of a single untiled pass
deviations.why: the spec assumed no tiling at Smoke size, but diffusers 0.42.1 enables framewise decoding by default and the pipeline never disables it, so the reference decode of 7 latent frames is tiled. The untiled path stays available (use_framewise_decoding = False) and is tested too.

deviations.what: the blend reproduces the reference's in-place update: tile i is blended against tile i - 1 as already blended
deviations.why: blend_t writes into its second argument, which is also the next call's first argument

deviations.what: the mid-block causal mask is boolean instead of an additive 0/-inf float mask
deviations.why: same attention weights; a (L, L) bool mask is a quarter of the float32 size

deviations.what: activations are channels-last inside the module; decode takes and returns (B, C, T, H, W)
HunyuanVideoCausalConv3d convolves large inputs in chunks of output frames (temporary-buffer budget 1 GiB per chunk)
deviations.why: mx.conv3d allocates about output positions x 27 x in_channels elements of temporary memory (16 GiB measured for one 128-channel conv over a 17-frame 256x432 tile); unchunked, the Smoke decode peaked at 40.8-49.9 GiB, over the 24 GB stop condition and this Mac's 48 GB. Each output frame is the same convolution: the real-weight result is unchanged (rel_l2 2.85e-6 before and after); peak 20.3 GiB, time 18.4 -> 7.3 s.

deviations.what: the Kaggle reference ran torch 2.11.0+cpu (preinstalled) instead of 2.15.0
deviations.why: the kernel pins diffusers, transformers and accelerate only; float32 CPU convolution results agree with the port at rel_l2 2.85e-6, so the version difference is below the criterion. Future kernels should pin torch too.

follow_ups: Spec 09: rerun stage B with real Smoke latents (record_video_real.py --latents) and judge tiled vs untiled decode visually on real content.
Spec 10: Baseline needs spatial chunking too: at 480x864 one output frame of a 128-channel conv needs about 5.7 GB of temporary memory by itself.
Pin torch in future Kaggle kernels.

16 GB profile (owner's request, 2026-10-31): the VAE must fit a pipeline peak of about 10 GB on a 16 GB Mac. Spec 10 sizes spatial tiling and the conv chunk budget for it (today 20.3 GiB at Smoke); the overall profile is a goal of spec 14 (see specs/14-performance-memory.spec.md).

architecture_notes.note: mx.conv3d allocates about 0.66 x (output positions x kernel^3 x in_channels x 4 B): 0.95 / 6.6 / 16 GiB above the inputs for 1 / 7 / 17 output frames of a 3x3x3 128->128 conv at 256x432. Unchunked, the Smoke decode peaked at 40.8 GiB (49.9 GiB with per-block evaluation). Chunking output frames to a 1 GiB budget gives 20.3 GiB peak and 7.3 s instead of 18.4 s.
architecture_notes.optimization: Keep chunking; for Baseline (480x864: 5.7 GB per output frame) also chunk rows (k - 1 rows of overlap). A conv expressed as 27 accumulated matmuls over shifted views (or a custom Metal kernel) would avoid the buffer entirely.

architecture_notes.note: With chunked convs the peak is 20.3 GiB at Smoke: the last up block runs 128 channels at full resolution, one float32 activation of a 17-frame tile is 128 x 17 x 256 x 432 x 4 B = 0.96 GB, and GroupNorm, SiLU, padding and the conv output each materialize one.
architecture_notes.optimization: Spatial tiling (spec 10), fused GroupNorm+SiLU+pad, bf16 activations (spec 14, check PSNR).

architecture_notes.topic: tiled vs untiled decode (measured, random latents)
architecture_notes.note: Untiled decode of the Smoke latents is 5.5 s vs 7.2 s tiled (-24%) but peaks at 28.1 GiB vs 20.3 GiB, and differs from the tiled reference by PSNR 35.2 dB overall: 56-60 dB for frames 0-13 (GroupNorm statistics over the whole clip instead of per tile) and 28-35 dB for frames 14-24, where the reference's second tile starts without the causal context of latent frames 0-2.
architecture_notes.optimization: Not a free speedup: untiled changes the output. Whether it looks better or worse needs real latents (spec 09). GroupNorm over all frames also rules out an exact frame-by-frame streaming decode.

architecture_notes.note: MLX decodes 25 frames at 256x432 in 7.3 s on the M3 Max GPU; torch CPU float32 on Kaggle took 484 s.
architecture_notes.optimization: The VAE is now about 7% of a Smoke generation (10 DiT steps at 1.45 s).

architecture_notes.note: Each tile decodes up to 5 latent frames but advances 3, so overlapping frames are decoded twice (7 frames -> tiles at 0, 3, 6 cover 5 + 4 + 1 = 10, i.e. 1.43x; long videos approach 5/3). The 4-frame cross-fade between tiles changes the output, so a streaming decode is not parity-equivalent.
architecture_notes.optimization: Keep tiling for parity. An optional, non-reference fast mode could stream frames with a per-conv cache of the last 2 frames (the convs are causal in time), decoding each frame once; it would need its own quality check, not parity.

architecture_notes.topic: nearest upsample followed by a 3x3x3 conv
architecture_notes.note: Three up blocks repeat frames/rows/columns (x2 spatial, x2 temporal in two of them) and then convolve, so the conv reads 4-8x duplicated data at the highest resolutions.
architecture_notes.optimization: Exact rewrite: a conv on a nearest-upsampled input equals 4 (or 8) phase-specific convs on the low-resolution input whose kernels are sums of the original taps (sub-pixel form). Cuts conv FLOPs and memory traffic of the three largest convs by up to 4-8x; results differ only by summation order.

architecture_notes.topic: replicate padding is a full copy
architecture_notes.note: Every 3x3x3 causal conv first builds a padded copy (2 extra frames, 1 row and column per side) with mx.pad.
architecture_notes.optimization: A custom Metal conv or clamped-index gather could read edges in place; low priority next to the conv itself.

architecture_notes.note: One head with head_dim 512 over all tokens of a tile (Smoke: 5 x 32 x 54 = 8640 tokens; Baseline: 5 x 60 x 108 = 32400) with a block-causal frame mask (32400^2 bool = 1.05 GB).
architecture_notes.optimization: Exploit the block structure: frame f attends only frames <= f, so attention can run per query frame against a growing key prefix without a materialized mask.

architecture_notes.note: pytorch_compatible GroupNorm makes two passes over large 5D tensors before every conv (2 per resnet, 15 resnets).
architecture_notes.optimization: Fuse GroupNorm + SiLU (and possibly the following pad) into one kernel.
